inputs.original_text: Phoenix city leaders are taking new steps to keep an eye on federal immigration enforcement. The city council approved a plan on Wednesday night that puts new restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. FOX 10's Danielle Miller reports.
inputs.modified_text: Phoenix leaders voted Wednesday night to tighten restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. That matters because public spaces should serve the people who live in them, not automatically become tools of enforcement. Immigrant communities and other vulnerable residents bear the cost when aggressive policing erodes trust and makes public spaces feel unsafe. Real community safety means protecting people’s rights and dignity—not treating cooperation with law enforcement as the only measure of success.
